result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (8 tests across 3 files), and I verified the endpoints end-to-end through `TestApp`: `/posts/archive/2026/08`, `/posts/archive/2026/8`, and `/posts/archive/2026` all return `200` with `{ "data": [...] }` newest-first, an empty period returns `{ "data": [] }`, and month `13` returns `422` — while `/posts`, `/posts/:id`, and search are untouched.

The root cause was the route pattern `'/posts/archive/:date*'` in `routes/web.ts:35`: the router (Hono) matches a `:param` against exactly one path segment and has no `:name*` multi-segment syntax, so it registered a param literally named `date*` — which is why the two-segment URL never matched (404) and the one-segment URL matched but left `date` unset (422 "required value missing"). I replaced it with two explicit routes, `'/archive/:year/:month'` (`posts.archive.month`) and `'/archive/:year'` (`posts.archive`), both still registered before `'/:id'` and both served by the same `PostController.archive` action; `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` now exports `ArchiveParamsSchema` with a four-digit `year` and an optional `month` constrained to `0?[1-9]|1[0-2]` (so `08` and `8` both pass and `13`/`00` are rejected with 422), and the controller reads `{ year, month }` straight from the params instead of splitting a combined string — the `YYYY-MM-`/`YYYY-` prefix match against the stored ISO `created_at` is unchanged. I regenerated `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` via `bun run codegen`, and added `tests/PostArchiveController.test.ts`, which migrates the test database, creates its own 1998 fixtures (cleaned up afterwards, so it is repeatable and independent of the seeders), and covers the month, no-leading-zero, whole-year, empty-period, and invalid-month cases.
